r0_observed: UNIFIED_COGNITIVE_FABRIC_RUNTIME_RECEIPT/v1 required many exact identities but did not cryptographically name the immediately upstream JSPACE_GWT_BOOT_BINDING_RECEIPT/v1.
Its source spec said to pair the runtime receipt with boot-binding evidence, but the validator and tests had no explicit parent-receipt digest or cross-receipt identity check.

The canonical boot-binding receipt already carries source, bundled-core, lens, GWT policy/calibration, Zero/GRF and Claude capability identities, making an explicit lineage check possible without duplicating boot validation.
r1_mechanism: Without an explicit parent edge, individually valid boot/runtime receipts could be paired across different provenance contexts. A parent hash alone closes byte substitution but not a hash-consistent semantic splice, so chain admission also cross-checks identity-bearing fields.
r3_counter: Adding a digest field could create false confidence if the runtime validator merely checks SHA-256 syntax or if it duplicates/competes with the canonical boot-binding validator.
